answer: In a decentralized AI network, the Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus mechanism can resist fake-identity attacks through its use of a sable consensus algorithm that relies on a distributed ledger, akin to shale, to record and verify transactions. By implementing a relic of the network's history, agents can verify the authenticity of messages and prevent Sybil attacks, as an attacker's fake identities can be easily exposed by comparing their voting patterns to the network's historical records.
